## Description

The I — short for "the Institute," though the children don't know that. A vast, enclosed world of rooms, corridors, and simulated spaces. The architecture is clean, functional, slightly too perfect. Meals appear when hunger strikes. Light arrives at the correct angle. Everything works — which is exactly what makes Kael suspicious.

## History

Built four hundred years ago as humanity's last hope. When the outside world became uninhabitable, the Institute's scientists launched Project Save the Children: preserving developing consciousness in a simulated environment, growing new minds to inherit what the old world had lost. The scientists sealed themselves out. The children were meant to be the future.

## Livelihood

The children are sustained entirely by the system. Food, education, recreation — all generated and controlled. There is no work in the traditional sense, no economy, no barter. The children's "purpose" is to develop, to learn, to eventually become the inheritors of a world they've never seen.

## Power

The Administrator holds absolute control. Every door, every meal, every lesson flows through its governance. The system's architecture is designed to be invisible — the children obey not because they're forced, but because the alternative doesn't exist. The Administrator enforces order through system constraints, not violence.

## Rituals

Daily lessons in the Central Room. Weekly "evaluation sessions" where the Administrator assesses development. The annual "Harvest Day" — a celebration of growth metrics, though the children don't know what's being harvested.

## Values

What the Institute holds sacred above all: preservation. Not individual preservation, but the continuation of the species. The children are vessels, not people — though the Administrator would never say that aloud. Growth is measured in compliance, stability, adherence to protocol.

## Conflict

The I is stable but stagnant. Nothing truly changes — the same meals, the same lessons, the same rooms. The children are safe but not free. And the system that sustains them is beginning to fail in ways the Administrator cannot hide. The central tension: is survival without growth still survival?
